Jordan: Heads-up — customer org_42 reported their monthly token bucket hit 0 mid-run during a 2hr livestream and stayed at 0 until the nightly refill. They claim they were nowhere near the 1M/month limit earlier. They saw continuous 429s from ~10:20–10:40. Any ideas?
Maria: Can you drop org id + a couple request IDs? Also what's their plan and timezone?
Jordan: org_42. sample req ids: req_abc123, req_def456. Plan = Pro (1M tokens/month). They're US-PST. Usage graph shows a big spike 10:12–10:45 and a bunch of retries. UI displayed 0 at ~10:30 but some billing events show `quota.consume` successes just before that. Snippet: ```2026-02-15T10:29:58Z INFO quota.consume org=org_42 req=req_abc123 tokens=+0 status=LIMIT_REACHED
2026-02-15T10:30:01Z INFO billing.event org=org_42 event=monthly_refill scheduled=00:00:00Z```
Maria: Hmm — could be a propagation/cache issue where the refill or usage weren't visible to the API edge. @henry can you take a look at refill job + cache layer? :eyes: 
Henry: On it. Initial check: monthly refill job ran at 00:00 UTC as expected. Customer in PST means refill visible at 16:00 local. I also see a Redis failover around 10:25 UTC correlated with a high retry rate from their client. Our edge quota cache TTL is 5s; if failover caused some edges to miss the updated token balance, edges would keep returning 429s until cache warmed.
Jordan: So the "visible zero" could be the UI edge showing stale state while backend refill had or hadn't happened? But the API kept returning 429s during that window. Repro idea: 1) long-running websocket or livestream -> continuous token drain, 2) client retries aggressively on 429 -> bursts of `consume` requests, 3) Redis failover or transient cache miss during refill -> edges not seeing latest balance, 4) edges keep serving 429 despite central state flip.
Maria: Actionable mitigation: immediate — we can issue a manual goodwill top-up and advise customer to apply exponential backoff on retries. Short term infra — add a cache-warmup propagation step on monthly refill (push invalidation to edges). Product/UX — smooth UI to avoid showing hard zero during brief propagation windows. @Priya (Billing) can we offer a one-off top-up? :thinking: 
Priya (Billing): I can do a 50k token manual top-up as goodwill. Need billing contact + ticket reference. I can also flag account so it doesn't get auto-throttled for 24h while we investigate.
Henry: I'll file an infra incident: include Redis failover timeline, edge cache miss metrics, and implement urgent fix to broadcast refills to edges and introduce a short grace window (allow 1 in-flight token request to succeed if refill was recorded in last X seconds). Also adding guardrails to avoid retry storms turning into effective denial-of-service.
Jordan: Thanks — I'll tell the customer: manual top-up + flag, ask them for websocket session IDs and retry client logs. TL;DR for internal notes: customer saw quota exhaustion due to combination of retry storm + cache propagation lag during a transient Redis failover. Next steps: top-up, infra cache-invalidation on refill, UX smoothing, recommend client backoff. :thumbsup:
Maria: I'll create support ticket with summaries + assign to infra and billing. Closing loop once infra PR and billing action complete.
